editorial:
Imagine a world where the dad is basically a big kid and the son has to be the grown-up. That is exactly what you get with this wild ride through 1920s Kansas. You follow Eli, a stunt pilot who flies all over the place, and his eleven-year-old son, Rodger. They are on a mission to reach a legendary place called San Willow, but the journey is really about their strange bond. It is a mix of high-flying adventure and some pretty sad moments, as you see a young boy dealing with the loss of his mother while keeping his reckless father out of trouble. 

What really works here is the acting, especially the way the kid plays someone way too mature for his age. You will find the pacing a bit slow in some spots, and the drama gets heavy when Rodger struggles with his emotions at night. However, the old-school plane stunts are a blast to watch. If you enjoy character studies with a bit of a vintage feel, you should definitely check this out. It is best experienced by adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or you can try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: As the journey wraps up, you see that San Willow was more of a dream than a real destination. The movie ends with Eli and Rodger finally finding a sense of peace with each other. Eli starts to grow up a little bit, and Rodger finds some comfort after grieving for his mom. They realize that their relationship is more important than any place on a map, ending their trip with a stronger bond.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage aviation and stories about unlikely family bonds.
